clue.text: Stop! Fold right away

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so the named letter comes out of the word

blocks.note: a fold in cloth or paper is a crease
R is the standard abbreviation for right; it is the letter taken out

explanation.surface: Someone barks orders: stop, fold, right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'immediately', but it means remove the R from CREASE, leaving CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to halt, and the imperative 'Cease!' is an order to stop.

clue.text: PDQ's musical proficiency?

blocks.note: first meaning: PDQ is short for 'pretty damn quick', an urgent call for speed
second meaning, playfully: a jazz player's technical skill is called their chops, so doubled chops is lots of skill

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as a pun: 'chops' is musicians' slang for technique, and the answer is that word said twice. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal command meaning hurry up, the same urgency as pretty damn quick.

clue.text: Frank rising up in support of worker's organ

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the other one

blocks.note: the worker ant is the classic crossword worker
Anne Frank, the diarist; her first name is written backwards here

explanation.surface: An honest union member stands up for a worker's mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like an adjective meaning candid; it is the surname that leads to Anne. Fittingly, the antenna belongs to the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a sensory organ on an insect's head.

clue.text: Windows release obscured by eeriest, arcane knowledge

indicators.note: something obscured by another thing is wrapped up inside it
arcane suggests something mysterious and cryptic, so the letters are scrambled beyond recognition

blocks.note: Windows XP was a version of Microsoft's operating system
taken as written

explanation.surface: A software update is hidden behind spooky, esoteric lore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arcane knowledge' reads as one phrase, but 'arcane' is the anagram signal and 'knowledge' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skill and know-how in a field, a close synonym for knowledge.

clue.text: Essential components of some engines: creamed corn (I jest)

indicators.note: creamed corn has been mashed to a pulp, so the letters that follow are mashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A joker claims some engines run on creamed corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creamed corn' looks like a single food item, but 'creamed' is the signal and only 'corn' plus 'I jest' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuel injectors spray fuel into the cylinders of diesel and fuel-injected petrol engines, so those engines cannot run without them.

clue.text: Perfect passenger to ride along

indicators.note: a passenger is carried inside a vehicle, so the answer travels inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone praises the perfect passenger to take along on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal and perfect are synonyms, both meaning as good as can be.

clue.text: Jam with rock musician Morton

blocks.note: in American usage jelly is a fruit spread like jam
to rock and to roll are both to sway from side to side

explanation.surface: A jam session with a rock musician named Morton.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'rock musician' together, but rock is wordplay and the musician is Morton.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly Roll Morton was the early New Orleans jazz pianist and composer, so the musician's nickname is the answer.

clue.text: 8⅓-foot piece of cake?

blocks.note: eight and a third feet is a hundred inches: C, the Roman numeral for 100, followed by INCH

explanation.surface: A cake slice over eight feet long, presumably for a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the length into inches: 8⅓ × 12 = 100, and 100 is C in Roman numerals, so a hundred inches is C INCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something very easy, and a cinch is exactly that.

clue.text: Laundry additive is unopened more frequently

indicators.note: something unopened has not had its front broken into; here the opening letter is simply missing

blocks.note: fabric softener is added to a wash to make clothes feel softer

explanation.surface: A complaint that the fabric softener sits unopened more often than not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laundry additive' looks like the definition, but it is the word that loses its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Oftener is the comparative of often, so it means more frequently.

clue.text: Friendly note involving spies

indicators.note: a thing involving another takes it in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: sol is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A friendly message that has the spies mixed up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Social describes a person who enjoys company, a near synonym of friendly and sociable.

clue.text: Yokel put cows back, sheltering eight times as many

indicators.note: the words shelter the answer, holding it inside their run of letters
back tells you to read that run of letters from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words, read in clue order

explanation.surface: A farmhand drives the herd back into a barn with room for eight times as many animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word looks like a farmyard instruction to solve, but the answer sits backwards inside yokEL PUT CO-ws.
explanation.definitionFit: Octuple means multiplied by eight, an eightfold quantity.

clue.text: Crazy, mixed-up aunt sits in lap, mostly

indicators.note: something mixed up is jumbled, so the word's letters are reordered
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to sit in something is to be placed inside it

blocks.note: a cat laps or licks its milk; dropping the end leaves LIC
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dotty relative perched on somebody's knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lap' looks like the knee-top a person sits on; it is the verb for drinking like a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is a madman, and the word also works as an adjective for crazy or wildly foolish.

clue.text: Penny leads a demonstration downtown

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so this piece is placed before the other

blocks.note: an American penny is a cent
a rally is a mass protest or demonstration

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny heads a protest march in the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name heading the march; it is the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown means in a city's central area, so used as an adverb it matches centrally, in the middle.

clue.text: Prosecutor goes after precious car

indicators.note: going after means following, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment like precious
a DA is a district attorney, the US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A prosecutor pursues somebody's prized automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' reads as an adjective for the car; it is a pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: Honda is a Japanese manufacturer, so a Honda is an example of a car.

clue.text: African animal is well ahead of a detective

indicators.note: being ahead of something places it first in line

blocks.note: well, as in in good health, is OK
taken as written
a PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: An African beast is well ahead of the detective tracking it.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a striped forest mammal of Congo, a relative of the giraffe, so it is an example of African fauna.

clue.text: 500 kids returning around current winter migrant

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so these letters are read in the opposite direction
around means surrounding, so the outer letters enclose another piece

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to kid someone is to rib or tease them
current means present, happening now

explanation.surface: Five hundred children circling back around a seasonal visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids' looks like children; it is the verb meaning teases. In American usage a snowbird is a northerner who goes south for the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowbird is a person, often retired, who spends winter in a warm southern state, a human seasonal migrant.

clue.text: Woman eating fruit with commercial pioneer

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other
with here simply adds the next piece alongside

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
a pear is a fruit
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A woman munching fruit beside an advertising trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial pioneer' reads as a business innovator; 'commercial' is wordplay and 'pioneer' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the person or group leading an advance, so it names a pioneer or trailblazer.

clue.text: Type of curve enveloping John Washington: it can be white and protective

definitions.text: it can be white and protective

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the outer word encloses the others

blocks.note: the bell curve is the normal distribution graph
a john is a toilet, and so is a loo
Washington, DC is the US capital

explanation.surface: A curve shaped round a man named John Washington, then a hint about something white and protective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Washington' reads as one person's name; it is two pieces, a toilet and the capital's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: White blood cells are part of the immune system, so a blood cell can be white and protective.

clue.text: To make a long story short: stupid scam comes first

definitions.text: To make a long story short

indicators.note: coming first puts this piece at the front of the line

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or scam
dense means slow-witted

explanation.surface: A storyteller cuts to the chase: it was a dumb scheme first of all.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to shorten or abridge, which is what making a long story short does.

clue.text: Border kind of property of the stars

blocks.note: a side is an edge or border
real property is land and buildings, as in real estate

explanation.surface: A boundary fixes the kind of property movie stars own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomical adjective for things measured against the fixed stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: Tasteless fool lives with Nickelback

indicators.note: back tacked on the end of the band's name sends everything before it the other way

blocks.note: a dip is a dope, a foolish person
lives in the sense exists, which is is
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel; the tail of the band's name is the reversal signal

explanation.surface: A dull fool shares a house with the rock band Nickelback.
explanation.walkthrough: Nickelback, a Canadian rock band often mocked as bland, splits into Nickel plus a reversal signal applied to the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour, so food without taste is insipid.

clue.text: Leaders of organized unions try delivering our best

indicators.note: the leaders of a line of words are their front letters

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Union organizers set out to deliver their best effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like a noun meaning top effort; it is the verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them, which is what to outdo means.

clue.text: Activates unit around containers

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: a ton is a unit of weight
urns are vessels

explanation.surface: A device switches on a unit placed around some containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Turns on is the phrasal verb for switching something on, which is to activate it.

clue.text: Vocation of horse's ass: interrupting someone who gives a damn

indicators.note: the ass of a horse is its rear end, so only the final letter of the word is kept
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: a carer is one who cares, someone who gives a damn
the tail-end letter

explanation.surface: Choosing a job as a horse's ass, butting in on someone who actually cares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse's ass' sounds like an insult; it means the back end of the word horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a person's chosen profession or calling, a synonym of vocation.

clue.text: Parts of a church expunging foremost of errors

indicators.note: expunging the foremost means wiping out the very front letter

blocks.note: lapses are slips or errors

explanation.surface: Church sections being cleaned up by removing mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Diving from small island

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: Diving off a little island.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba is the self-contained breathing apparatus, and scuba is used as shorthand for that kind of diving.

clue.text: Redo components, repeating some in a new sequence

indicators.note: taking a word as its components treats it as loose parts to be put together in any order

blocks.note: taken as written
some of those letters used again: two more R, two more E and one more D

explanation.surface: Instructions to rebuild the parts, reusing some, in a fresh order.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is built only from the four letters of REDO, some used several times, and the clue says just that.
explanation.definitionFit: Reordered means arranged again, so things reordered are placed in a new sequence.

clue.text: Chose large reference work about Barnum

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: the Oxford English Dictionary, a famously large reference work
P. T. Barnum, the American showman

explanation.surface: Someone picked a giant reference book about the circus showman.
explanation.definitionFit: Opted is the past tense of opt, to pick from alternatives, which is what chose means.

clue.text: Embrace supernatural powers and love to do drugs

blocks.note: ESP is extrasensory perception
love is zero in tennis, written O
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: A seeker embraces psychic powers, love and drug-taking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embrace' looks like a hug; it is the sense of adopting a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a belief is to adopt or support it, as to embrace an idea.

clue.text: True motivation for corrupt senator's betrayal

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoilt and twisted out of its proper form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inquiry into why a crooked senator turned traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words dress the clue: the corrupt senator's letters really are what lies behind the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest kind of betrayal.

clue.text: How one might be caught, holding no spades or clubs?

definitions.text: How one might be caught, holding no spades or clubs?

blocks.note: surface reading: the manner of being caught in the act of a crime
card reading: a bridge hand with only hearts and diamonds, the suits of one colour

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a card-table joke on the idiom for being caught in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught in the act of wrongdoing is the idiom, and a card hand with only hearts and diamonds is literally all one colour.

clue.text: Armstrong's unusually clean weapon

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are not in their normal order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at cyclist Lance Armstrong, whose clean record was unusual and whose weapon was doping.
explanation.walkthrough: Armstrong's first name is the answer, an extra hint; the cyclist was stripped of his titles for doping, so 'unusually clean' is a joke too.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight, a weapon.
